The register says applicant is "Zhonghang Electronicc Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd." (note "Electronicc" — likely a typo of "Electronics" but that's the register value). The document says "Zemic Europe B.V."

Zemic Europe B.V. is actually a real company — Zemic is a brand related to Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments (ZEMIC stands for Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments). Zemic Europe B.V. is the European subsidiary/distributor based in the Netherlands. So are they the same entity? Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd. is the Chinese manufacturer (ZEMIC). Zemic Europe B.V. is a separate legal entity (the Dutch subsidiary). These are genuinely different legal entities — a parent and its subsidiary are different companies.

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

The names are not spelling drift of each other — "Zemic Europe B.V." vs "Zhonghang Electronicc Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd." are different company names. Even though related (ZEMIC is the brand of Zhonghang), they are distinct legal entities. The certificate document is the legal instrument, so best_value = "Zemic Europe B.V."

So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Zemic Europe B.V.".

Why: The document names a distinct legal entity (Zemic Europe B.V., the Dutch subsidiary) rather than a spelling variant of the register's Chinese parent, so the certificate's own applicant governs.
